Subject: Initial: retention carveout request and sample logs

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — I’m Danielle in procurement/security at MedSprout. As part of our SIG/SOC2 evidence collection we need two things clarified before we move to PO: (1) confirmation of your deletion workflow and evidence that customer-scoped logs with PHI can be selectively retained for longer than our default TTL under an exception; (2) a small sample of the actual log manifest format so our engineers can validate parsing and redaction.

To be explicit: we might need a 180-day retention carveout for a single tenant (our production tenant) while maintaining deletion guarantees for others. Can you confirm if Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention overrides + how you gate exceptions? Also please tell us what evidence you can provide (retention config snapshot, signed exception addendum, redaction proof) and typical lead time.

I can share a sample CSV of the fields we need to verify — attaching a manifest in my next message.

Thanks,
Danielle

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we support tenant-scoped retention overrides and an exceptions workflow that produces signed addenda + audit evidence. Below is a concise runbook and the items we typically provide. I’ve looped in Neha (security) for the technical evidence and Jordan/Ben for legal/procurement cadence.

Planned deliverables if you want a 180-day tenant override for only your production tenant:
- Signed addendum template (DocuSign) listing the tenant ID and retention window (can be scoped to a single tenant).
- Snapshot of retention config (signed and timestamped export) showing TTL change for the tenant.
- Deletion proof: sample deletion job run logs and MD5 manifest showing objects targeted and confirmation of deletion in object store.
- For PHI: redaction pipeline transcript + redaction checksums where full events were redacted before long-term storage.

Questions from our side to scope the work:
1) Is the data you're asking to keep full event payloads or a reduced telemetry index?
2) Do you require immutable/forensics-grade copies (WORM) or simply extended TTL with auditing?
3) Any legal hold windows already in place that would supersede 180 days?

If you can attach the CSV manifest you mentioned (field names + example rows) we’ll produce a mapping template and quick smoke run to show how redaction/TTL will apply. Typical lead time to produce the evidence pack is 5–7 business days after we get the manifest and confirm scope; add 3–5 business days if we need a legal addendum signed.

Next steps: please send the manifest; Neha will propose a minimal evidence checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Evidence checklist & technical approach for tenant-scoped retention override

Hi all — quick technical note from security/operations. TL;DR: we can implement a per-tenant 180-day TTL override and provide verifiable deletion evidence if the retention exception is authorized by your legal/procurement and our security team. Below are the exact pieces we can provide and the controls that will remain in place.

What we can provide (evidence items):
- Config snapshot: the retention rule object (JSON) as exported from the control plane, signed and timestamped.
- Audit log extract: all API calls that created/modified the rule and the operator accounts (with request IDs).
- Deletion job audit: run-id, target manifest (list of object ids), and post-run verification that object metadata shows deleted=true.
- Redaction transcript: when payloads contain PHI we run our redaction pipeline; we can provide the pre/post checksums and a redaction log for sampling.
- SIG/CAIQ mapping: note where this exception maps to specific CAIQ/SIG sections around data retention and customer delegation.

Operational constraints and controls we require:
- Exception is scoped by tenant ID and start/end dates; it cannot be retroactively applied to previously purged cold objects.
- All evidence packages will redact third-party customer data except the tenant requested; we will provide sampling only (we do not export full PHI sets).
- KMS-wrapped keys: any retained objects will remain encrypted under customer or Redwood-managed KMS (TBD).

Minimal evidence checklist for MedSprout to sign-off (we ask you to confirm these items):
1) Tenant ID (production) to apply the override to.
2) Exact retention start/end date (we’ll default to start=addendum signing date).
3) Whether you want WORM-style immutability or extended TTL with audit logs.
4) Contact for on-call evidence review (name/email).

I’m dropping a short runbook snippet that ops will use to produce the deletion verification (attached PDF). If you can attach the manifest CSV we’ll run it against a staging snapshot and return a redaction sample + TTL-change snapshot.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
